items.title: The Four Engagements Defined: Taming, Moistening, Generating Pliancy, and Purifying Insight

items.zh: 云何調練心作意？謂由此作意，於可厭患法令心厭離，是名調練心作意。云何滋潤心作意？謂由此作意，於可欣尚法令心欣樂，是名滋潤心作意。
items.en: What is the mental engagement of taming the mind? That is, through this engagement, one causes the mind to become revulsed towards loathsome things — this is called the mental engagement of taming the mind. What is the mental engagement of moistening the mind? That is, through this engagement, one causes the mind to delight in esteemed things — this is called the mental engagement of moistening the mind.

items.zh: 云何生輕安作意？謂由此作意，於時時間，於可厭法令心厭離；於時時間，於可欣法令心欣樂已；安住內寂靜、無相、無分別中，一境念轉。由是因緣，對治一切身心麁重，能令一切身心適悅，生起一切身心輕安。是名生輕安作意。云何淨智見作意？謂由此作意，於時時間，即用如是內心寂靜為所依止，由內靜心數數加行，於法觀中修增上慧，是名淨智見作意。
items.en: What is the mental engagement of generating pliancy? That is, through this engagement, at fitting times one causes the mind to become revulsed towards loathsome things, and at fitting times one causes the mind to delight in esteemed things; having done so, one abides in inward stillness, free of marks, free of discursive thought, with mindfulness continuing on a single object. Through this, one counters all bodily and mental heaviness, brings all body and mind to ease, and gives rise to complete bodily and mental pliancy. What is the mental engagement of purifying wisdom and insight? That is, through this engagement, at fitting times, relying precisely on that same inward stillness, through repeated inward application one cultivates superior wisdom within contemplation of phenomena — this is called the mental engagement of purifying wisdom and insight.

items.zh: 彼修行者，於時時間，於可厭法令心厭離；如是於漏及漏處法，能令其心生熱、等熱，生厭、等厭。

items.title: Four Objects of Loathing, Three Objects of Esteem

items.zh: 何等名為可厭患處？略有四種可厭患處。謂自衰損及他衰損，現在會遇正現前時，如理作意數思惟故，成可厭處。若自興盛及他興盛，過去盡滅離變壞時，如理作意數思惟故，成可厭處。
items.en: What is called a loathsome object? There are, in brief, four kinds of loathsome object: one's own decline and another's decline, when actually encountered and directly present, become, through repeated sound-reasoning attention, a loathsome object; and one's own flourishing and another's flourishing, when they have entirely passed away, ceased, departed, or degraded, become, through repeated sound-reasoning attention, a loathsome object.

items.zh: 即彼行者，於時時間，於可欣法令心欣樂；如是於彼生欣樂故，能令其心極成津潤，融適澄淨。何等名為可欣尚處？
略有三種可欣尚處。一者、三寶；二者、學處清淨、尸羅清淨；三者、於自所證差別，深生信解，心無怯弱。
items.en: There are, in brief, three kinds of esteemed object: first, the Three Jewels; second, purity of the precepts one has undertaken; third, deep confidence and understanding, free of timidity, regarding the various things one has personally attained.

items.zh: 云何隨念三寶，令心欣樂？

items.title: Section: The Triple Gem as Object of Esteem

items.zh: 謂作是念：我今善得如是大利，謂蒙如來應正等覺為我大師。我今善得如是大利，謂善說法毘柰耶中，我得出家。我今善得如是大利，謂我與諸具戒、具德、忍辱、柔和、成賢善法同梵行者共為法侶。我今當得賢善命終、賢善殞沒，當得賢善趣於後世。
items.en: One reflects thus: "I have now truly gained such great benefit — that the Tathāgata, the Worthy One, the Perfectly Enlightened One, is my great teacher. I have now truly gained such great benefit — that I have been able to go forth within the well-taught Dharma and discipline. I have now truly gained such great benefit — that I have, as fellow companions in the path, those of pure precepts, virtue, patience, and gentleness, who accord with the wholesome Dharma." "I shall attain a good death, a good passing, and shall attain a good destination in the life to come."

items.zh: 如是名為隨念三寶，令心欣樂。云何隨念學處清淨、尸羅清淨，令心欣樂？

items.title: Precept Purity and Confidence in One's Own Attainment

items.zh: 謂作是念：我今善得如是大利，謂於如來應正等覺大師、善說法毘柰耶、善修正行聲聞眾中，我得與彼同梵行者，同戒、同學、同修慈仁身語意業、同其所見、同所受用。如是名為隨念學處清淨、尸羅清淨，令心欣樂。謂無悔為先，發生歡喜。
items.en: One reflects thus: "I have now truly gained such great benefit — that, within the community of the Tathāgata, the Worthy One, the Perfectly Enlightened One, the well-taught Dharma and discipline, and those who rightly practice correct conduct, I share the same precepts, the same training, the same cultivation of loving-kindness in body, speech, and mind, the same views, and the same use of resources with my fellow practitioners of the pure life." … That is, freedom from regret comes first, and from it, joy arises.

items.zh: 云何於自所證差別，深生信解，心無怯弱處，令心欣樂？
謂作是念：我今有力、有所堪能，尸羅清淨，堪為法器。得與如是同梵行者同清淨戒，得與有智正至善士同其所見，我有堪能精勤修習如是正行。於現法中，能得未得、能觸未觸、能證未證。由是令心生大歡喜。
items.en: One reflects thus: "I now have strength, I have capability; my precepts are pure, and I am fit to be a vessel for the Dharma. I am able to share pure precepts with such fellow practitioners of the pure life, and to share the same views with wise, correctly arrived, virtuous persons. I am capable of diligently cultivating such correct conduct — and in this very life, able to attain what is not yet attained, to touch what is not yet touched, to realise what is not yet realised." Through this, great joy arises in the mind.

items.zh: 如是名為於自所證差別，深生信解，心無怯弱處，令心欣樂。又由前後勇猛精進，已得安住所證差別；由隨念此，復於後時所證差別，深生信解，令心欣樂。是名異門。彼修行者，於可厭法調練其心，於能隨順諸漏處法令心不向，違逆、棄背、離隔而住；於可欣法悅潤其心，於出、於離所生諸法有親愛故，令心趣向，附著、喜樂、和合而住。如是彼心由厭、由欣二種行相，背諸黑品，向諸白品，易脫而轉。其心如是背諸黑品，由調練心作意故。向諸白品，由滋潤心作意故。於時時間，依奢摩他內攝持心，由生輕安作意故。於時時間，於法思擇、最極思擇、周遍尋思、周遍伺察，由淨智見作意故。如是彼心，於時時間，為奢摩他、毘鉢舍那之所攝受，堪能與彼一切行相、一切功德作攝受因，經歷彼彼日夜、剎那、臘縛、須臾，逮得勝進。譬如黠慧鍛金銀師，或彼弟子，於時時間燒鍊金銀，令其棄捨一切垢穢；於時時間投清冷水，令於彼彼莊嚴具業，有所堪任，調柔隨順。於是黠慧鍛金銀師，或彼弟子，以其相似妙工巧智善了知已，用作業具，隨其所樂莊嚴具中，種種轉變。如是勤修瑜伽行者，為令其心棄背貪等一切垢穢，及令棄背染污憂惱，於可厭法深生厭離；為令趣向所有清淨善品喜樂，於可欣法發生欣樂。於是行者，隨於彼彼欲自安立，或奢摩他品、或毘鉢舍那品，即於彼彼能善親附，能善和合，無轉無動；隨其所樂種種義中，如所信解，皆能成辦。

blocks.text: The fifth locus: four kinds of attention that tame and nourish the mind. The fascicle ends with a long passage (0459a15) that Ru-Yi did not translate; it is summarised below.

**Taming** the mind: making it turn away from what should be loathed. **Moistening** the mind: making it delight in what should be esteemed. **Generating pliancy**: at fitting times loathing, at fitting times delighting, then abiding in inner stillness. **Purifying insight**: at fitting times examining phenomena.
"One's own decline and another's decline, when actually encountered": and "one's own flourishing and another's flourishing", seen as impermanent and leading to heedlessness.

The Three Jewels; the purity of one's precepts; "deep confidence, free of timidity, regarding what one has personally attained". "I have truly gained great benefit: that the Tathāgata is my great teacher; that I have gone forth within the well-taught Dharma; that I share the same precepts and views with those who practise rightly." Such a one will "attain a good death, a good passing".

Recollecting one's own attainments also gladdens the mind. Turning away from what leads to the corruptions and towards what leads to freedom, the mind "turns away from the dark and towards the bright, easily and freely". At times calm gathers it, at times insight examines it. The treatise compares this to a skilled goldsmith: at times he heats the gold to burn away impurities, at times plunges it in cold water, until it is pliant and can be worked into any ornament he wishes. So the practitioner, through loathing and delight, calm and insight, makes the mind workable for whatever he wishes to accomplish.

The six-fold investigation, nine good practices, four obstructions, and four kinds of attention. Fascicle 32 continues the third yogic process with the seven attentions and the attainment of the first absorption.

quiz.q: What image does Venerable Miào Jìng use for "moistening the mind"?
options: watering a parched plant regularly until it flourishes
quiz.why: "What is the mental engagement of moistening the mind? Through this engagement, one causes the mind to delight in esteemed things." Venerable Miào Jìng: like regularly watering something that was parched — it flourishes.

quiz.q: How does Venerable Miào Jìng put "one's own decline and another's" in plain words?
quiz.why: "One's own decline and another's decline, when actually encountered and directly present, become, through repeated sound-reasoning attention, a loathsome object." Venerable Miào Jìng: in our words, it's bad luck — that is decline.

quiz.q: "A good death, a good passing, a good destination" — how do the lectures distinguish these three?
options: Miào Jìng: arhatship is a good death, first through third fruits a good passing; Cháng Bǎi notes the Pixunji reads "good destination" differently from Miào Jìng
quiz.why: "I shall attain a good death, a good passing, and shall attain a good destination in the life to come." Venerable Miào Jìng: attaining arhatship is a good death; attaining the third, second, or first fruit is a good passing. Master Cháng Bǎi: "attaining a good destination in the next life" — the Pixunji explains this somewhat differently from Venerable Miào Jìng.
